findings.explanation: Items of the same kind in one list or stack are separated by different gaps, which reads as grouping that isn't there and makes the list look broken.
findings.recommendation: Give the container one gap (flex/grid `gap`, or one margin rule for all items) instead of per-item margins.

raised.title: Thick coloured stripe on one side
raised.why: A 3 px+ coloured border down one edge of cards, list items or alerts is a template habit.
raised.ask: Mark state or category with an icon, a label or the surface colour; if a stripe is part of the identity, accept it.

raised.title: Cards nested in cards
raised.why: A padded, rounded, bordered box inside another one adds frames without adding structure.
raised.ask: Flatten the inner level: separate with spacing, a divider or a heading instead of a second container.

raised.title: Emoji standing in for icons
raised.why: Emoji render differently on every platform and never match the interface's stroke, weight or palette.
raised.ask: Use one drawn icon set (authored SVG in the project's style, e.g. made with VectorCraft) at one stroke weight.

raised.title: Eyebrow label above a heading
raised.why: A small tracked-out uppercase kicker over every heading is a template rhythm, and the heading usually says it already.
raised.ask: Delete the label and let the heading carry the section; keep a label only when it carries information the heading does not.

raised.title: One default sans for everything
raised.why: Nearly all text is set in a default UI face (Inter, Roboto, Arial, the system font): no typographic voice of its own.
raised.ask: Choose a display face that belongs to the product's world and pair it with a readable text face; keep the default only if the identity calls for it.

limits: Every viewport is browser emulation (Playwright + Chromium 153.0.8010.12); iPhone sizes are CSS pixels and safe-area insets are emulated through CDP (Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride). Safari-specific rendering (WebKit), the real on-screen keyboard and physical reach are not reproduced.
Browser chrome: the first screen is re-measured with the viewport shortened by 120 px (Safari's toolbars); dynamic toolbar collapse is not reproduced.
Keyboard interference: fields that would zoom on focus (font-size < 16 px) are measured; whether the on-screen keyboard covers a field is not testable in emulation.
Hover/pressed/focus states are sampled once per visual variant of control; focus visibility comes from real Tab presses (desktop).
Canvas-drawn interfaces (games): the DOM does not describe what is drawn, so DOM-geometry metrics cover only the HTML overlay (HUD, menus); use judgements for the canvas.
No physical-device evidence: findings are emulation results, not device results.

comparison.why: same method, same screens, viewports and journeys; deltas use only metrics measured in both runs
